title: Tenali Raman Tale 121 (हिन्दी)
summary: Two forest dwellers, a humble tribal honey-gatherer named Kanna and a wealthy, smooth-talking village trader named Somappa, appeared befo... [HI]
full_text:
Two forest dwellers, a humble tribal honey-gatherer named Kanna and a wealthy, smooth-talking village trader named Somappa, appeared before King Krishnadevaraya's court disputing ownership of an enormous, thirty-pound wild forest honeycomb harvested from the cliff face of Mount Matanga.
The honey was rare, fragrant with wild mountain lotus, and worth fifty silver coins.

Somappa swore: 'I found the hive, climbed the cliff, and harvested the honey with my own hands! Kanna stole the basket from my cart!'
Kanna wept: 'Maharaj, climbing the cliff is the hereditary trade of my people! I gathered it at midnight!'

The King was perplexed, as both men described the mountain cliff accurately.
He asked Tenali Raman to resolve the dispute.

Tenali said: 'Maharaj, the proof is not in the honey, but in the hands that gathered it.'

Tenali commanded both men to step forward and hold out their bare arms and palms before the court.
Tenali inspected Somappa’s hands:
Somappa’s hands were soft, smooth, fair, with trimmed fingernails, completely unblemished by thorns or stings.

Tenali then inspected Kanna’s arms and hands:
Kanna’s palms were rough, calloused, and hardened like tree bark from climbing granite cliffs.
More importantly, across Kanna’s forearms and neck were dozens of fresh, swollen red bee stings, and small cuts from mountain brambles!

Tenali smiled and said to the court:
'Wild mountain cliff bees are fierce defenders of their hives; no human can harvest thirty pounds of wild comb without receiving dozens of stings and scratches!
Somappa’s hands are as smooth as a baby’s cheek; he never climbed a cliff or faced a bee in his life!
Kanna’s body carries the honorable scars of his dangerous labor!'

Faced with the undeniable evidence of his own unblemished palms, Somappa confessed that he had stolen the basket while Kanna was washing his stings in the mountain stream.
The King awarded the honeycomb to Kanna, along with a purse of silver, and fined Somappa fifty coins for false testimony.
The people cheered Tenali Raman, who proved that the scars of honest toil are the truest title deeds of labor.
moral: The true creator of wealth is proven by the scars of labor, not by the smooth palms of claimants. [HI]
